en: The *Běidǒu Qīxīng Húmó Fǎ* (Ritual of the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper for Homa) and the *Fù Chéngshèngguāng Fǎ* (Method for Restoring the Intense Radiance),
compiled by Yìxíng,
state that the mantra of the *Nengjíxiáng* (Auspicious Capable One) is as follows:

*Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo sumārasarvanokasatrarājāya. Tadyathā: Numati, pa-numati, sabhini-kṣe svāhā.* The mudrā of the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper (*Ursa Major*): Interlace the two fire fingers (the index fingers) and the two space fingers (the middle fingers) of the left and right hands; join the two water fingers (the ring fingers) in front, and extend the two earth fingers (the thumbs) and the two wind fingers (the little fingers). This immediately constitutes the mudrā. It is found in the *Ātmaparijñā-sūtra*, or as stated in the *Koujie* (Oral Instructions), and so forth.

The mantra is: Oṃ saptānarcir-ambare-jvala-pratāma-sarvami-namitra-kṣaṇa-bhava-tu svāhā. Regarding the seal of the Sun Deity (*Sūryadeva*): First join the palms, with the tips of the four fingers below the wind-fingers (the ring fingers) touching one another; open the two thumbs wide in front, each placed at the side of the wind-fingers (the index fingers). The mantra is as follows:

Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Namaḥ suriyasavanakṣatrarājāya | Oṃ amoghasyāmine śrīye svāhā || [The mudrā of the Moon Deity: With the hands in the *samādhi* position, join the fire and space fingers; extend the remaining fingers straight up as if holding a lotus flower. The mantra is: [as above].

Oṃ caṇḍāla-kṣatra-rāja nāma sidhya svāhā. This is the seal of Mars in the south. Form a fist with the left hand and place it at the waist; extend the five fingers of both hands straight up, touching each other, and bend the thumbs into the palms. For the mantra to summon [the deity] Svāhākāra, while the middle joints of the ring fingers are bent: [Mantra follows] *Note: The provided source text contains a complex sequence of Sanskrit phonemes and ritual instructions. The translation above renders the primary mantra and the description of the mudrā (hand gesture) and posture.*

Oṃ agarakāruṇiye svāhā. [This is] the seal of Varuṇa of the North. Form a fist with the right hand and place it at the waist; the left hand is bent into a fist with the fingers not entering the palm; the middle joints of the wind-finger (index finger) are held straight and slightly bent. The mantra is as follows: Oṃ agarakāruṇiye svāhā.

Oṃ mudgala-svāmin namaḥ svāhā. This is the seal of Jupiter (Bṛhaspati) in the east. With the two hands joined in the vajra-pañjali mudrā, extend the two thumbs upright. The mantra is as follows: [Oṃ mudgala-svāmin namaḥ svāhā].

Oṃ bharahasap-ti-nāma-pitavanyā-malavarodhini svāhā. (The mudrā for Venus in the western direction: join the two hands in *añjali*, with the two thumbs standing upright. The mantra is as follows: Oṃ bharahasap-ti-nāma-pitavanyā-malavarodhini svāhā.

Oṃ śukra-ga-dhara vara-vara-rajāya śrī-kali-svāhā. [This is the mudrā for Saturn in the central palace. First, join the palms; then, with the tips of the four fingers below the wind-fingers (the ring fingers) touching forward, open the two thumbs wide, each placed at the side of the wind-fingers. The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ vajra-ke-tu-nānākṣatra-rāja hūṃ svāhā. "Ke-tu" is translated as *dhvaja* (banner). A banner refers to a comet. *Rāhu* is the deity of conjunction and eclipses. For the two hidden stars [of Jupiter and Venus] and the three [planets] of wood, metal, and earth, all five use the same mudrā: join the two hands in *añjali*, with the two thumbs standing upright.

The General Seal of the Nine Planetary Devas (*Navagraha-deva*): With palms joined in the *tathāgata-puṣpamudrā*, the two thumbs are placed side by side and held upright; the two index fingers (*vāyu*) are extended, each opened toward its own base and held in the posture of coming and going. The general mantra is as follows: [Mantra follows]

Oṃ grahe śvariye prapātaya ṭiṭṭi māya svāhā. This is the general mudrā for the twenty-eight lunar mansions (*nakṣatras*). To perform it: join the palms firmly, extend both thumbs upright at the heart, and summon [the deities] with the two thumbs. The general mantra is as follows: Oṃ grahe śvariye prapātaya ṭiṭṭi māya svāhā.

Oṃ nakṣatranemisuvarṇaye svāhā. This is the mantra for summoning all the deities. The mudrā is as follows: form a fist with the right hand, extend the tip of the middle finger slightly, and bend it; this is the sign of summoning. The mantra is as stated above.
Oṃ sarvanarāyaṇāya īhe īḥ svāhā. The mantra for extending life is recited first one thousand times.

Oṃ vajrayuṣe amuka-sarvaha. The mudrā for the scented unguent (*vilepana*): With the wisdom hand turned outward, hold the wrist of the concentration hand upward and place it at the heart. The mantra for this is as follows:

Oṃ viśodhaya naṣṭāpavāsa svāhā. For the offering of flowers (*puṣpa*), perform the mudrā as follows: interlace the two hands with palms facing inward, then open them and turn them upward; join the tips of the sides of the two wind-fingers (*vāyu-aṅguli*) together, holding them empty at the edge of the wind-position at the heart. Recite this mantra: Oṃ viśodhaya naṣṭāpavāsa svāhā.

Oṃ mahā-maitryā-vyūha-ṇate svāhā. This is the incense mudrā: join the backs of the six fingers from the middle fingers downward so they touch; extend the two index fingers (vāyu) sideways so their tips do not touch slightly; place the thumbs at the sides of the [extended] index fingers at the heart. The mantra is as follows: [Mantra: Oṃ mahā-maitryā-vyūha-ṇate svāhā. This is the incense mudrā: join the backs of the six fingers from the middle fingers downward so they touch; extend the two index fingers (vāyu) sideways so their tips do not touch slightly; place the thumbs at the sides of the [extended] index fingers at the heart. The mantra is as follows.

Oṃ dharmadhātu-nirgate svāhā. This is the mantra for offering food. As for the mudrā: join the two hands empty-palmed, open them with the palms facing upward in the gesture of cupping, and place it at the heart while reciting this mantra.

Oṃ arara karara malinda namī malinda ne mahā-maṣṭi svāhā. The mudrā for the lamp-light: Form a fist with the right hand and press the tips of the index fingers toward the fire with the palms facing upward. The mantra for making offerings to the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper, one’s natal star, the lunar mansions (nakṣatras), the original spirits (yuanchen), and so forth, is as follows:

Oṃ tathāgatarājīśapraṇamya gaganodarya svāhā. The Seal of Universal Offering: Join the palms in the vajra-mudrā; form the two index fingers like a jewel (ratna) and extend the two thumbs side by side. The mantra is as follows: [Oṃ tathāgatarājīśapraṇamya gaganodarya svāhā].
Oṃ amoghapūjāmaṇipadmanavārī tathāgatavilocite samantaprasara hūṃ. [Praise Seal: Join the palms in the vajra-anjali mudrā.

*Āyantu devāḥ sagaṇasurakiṃnarā nāgāś ca yakṣāś ca pravaradharmagotrāḥ | Vidharma-jāpraśamacārīyāḥ | Nimantrayāmi tvāṃ bhūtapretān prākāśaya || Tad dhi śrīmān adhimānaḥ |* Within the incense burner, visualize seven *ru* syllables transforming into the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper (*Ursa Major*). Specifically, place the natal star (*janmanakṣatra*) in the center, with the other six stars as its attendants. Then, kneeling and joining the palms toward the burner, address it thus:
With a sincere heart, I reverently invoke the Seven Stars of the Northern Pole:
Tan-lang, Ju-men, Lu-cun, Wen-qu, Lien-cheng, Wu-qu, and the Honored Star Po-jun.
May they bring liberation from calamities and misfortunes for [Name], and may their lifespan be prolonged.
Having beheld you for a hundred autumns, I now perform this homa. I pray that the Honored Star descend to this place and accept this homa.
May the registers of death and calamity be erased, and may the tally of long life be inscribed. I cast this flower as my seat.

Form the mudrā of the Northern Dipper: with palms joined hollowly, join the two thumbs to press against the nails of the two ring fingers; let the two middle fingers form the shape of lotus petals; slightly open and bend the two index fingers, moving them back and forth. The mantra is as follows:

*Namo samantānārye he ci po i (1) ha i (2) na i (3) ka i (4) ra mo ra (5) tra ga (6) gaṃ (7) svāhā.* Visualize that the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper arrive. Next, having completed the offerings, perform the mudrā for casting flowers and dismissal: Join the palms with hollowed fingers; press the two thumbs against the nails of the two ring fingers; shape the middle and little fingers like a lotus; slightly open and bend the two index fingers outward to push them away. The mantra is as follows: *(Mantra follows)*

*Namo samanta-narāgra-pa-i-ha-i-ka-i-ra-mu-ra-ta-ra-ga-ha-ham svāhā.* Visualize the seven stars of the Northern Dipper and others returning to their original positions. The mantra for rectifying deficiencies is: *Oṃ hulu hulu jaya bhoje i svāhā*. For those who practice this homa ritual of the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper, their names shall be struck from the register of death, and records of long life shall be inscribed. Its divine efficacy is most manifest; there is no method for extending one’s life, increasing one’s years, eliminating calamities, and summoning wealth that is superior to this.

The Essential Dharma of the Blazing Light of the Northern Dipper. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha, residing in the palace of the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven, addressed the celestial deities, the lunar mansions, and the spirits of the twelve zodiacal signs.
I shall now proclaim the mantra of the Tathāgata Śālarāja of the past.

If there is a king whose realm is oppressed by the five planets or the twenty-eight lunar mansions, including the Imperial Throne, he should every morning at dawn within a maṇḍala form mudrās and recite this mantra seven times.

If the five planets and various luminaries threaten or oppress the various seats and are unable to cause calamity—should Mars intend to enter the Southern Dipper (Nandō)—one should place a dot in the shape of the Southern Dipper beneath an image of a wrathful deity (*krodharāja*), and within that, draw the form of that *setudhūru* (or *setudhura*) and write his name upon its heart. Then, forming the mudrā and placing it upon the body of the wrathful image, one should recite the mantra seven times.
By adding the name of that *śatru* (enemy) to the word *svāhā* and reciting the mantra with an angry and forceful voice, all calamities and misfortunes shall be removed.

*Namo samantabuddhānām* (1) *apraticchataśāsanebhyaḥ* (2) *oṃ* (3) *kha kha* (4) *khāhi khāhi* (5) *hūṃ hūṃ* (6) *jvala jvala* (7) *prajvala prajvala* (8) *tiṣṭha tiṣṭha* (9) *siddhri* (10) *sphoṭaya sphoṭaya* (11) *svāhā*. As for the mudrā: interlace the two hands with palms facing inward to form fists; extend the two middle fingers and join their tips together; bend the tips of the index fingers behind the middle fingers so that they resemble the shape of a vajra; and press the second joints of the middle fingers with the two thumbs.
This mantra is empowered by all the Tathāgatas.
This is called the Mantra of the Blazing Majestic Power of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa.
It is capable of accomplishing eighty thousand kinds of auspicious matters and can eliminate eighty thousand kinds of calamities, misfortunes, and evil dreams.
If one sees or hears of any inauspicious events, reciting this once with a pure mind will prevent them from causing harm.

If the five planets arrive at various seats, causing oppression, whether by entering, piercing through, or retrograding to invade them, one should add the name of that specific planet to the *śāpoha* verse.
Recite the mantra seven times and command those five planets that they may act for good and not cause harm.

Regarding the constellations and *bhūmipradeśas* (territorial divisions) reached by Mars, Venus, and the others, as well as the imperial seat within those *bhūmipradeśa*-constellations—one should, as before, draw the form of that malicious person beneath the image. This shall diminish that person so that they do not give rise to evil intentions. Or, when Rāhu eclipses the sun or moon, during solar or lunar occultations; or when a comet appears; or during droughts or floods.
Then, within the site of practice (maṇḍala) in a secluded place, one should wear black clothing and sit facing south.
Having burned dead ashes, one should draw a triangular altar and inscribe the forms of Rāhu, comets, and so forth therein.
During times of drought or excessive rain, one should draw the form of a dragon. Write the person's name upon its heart.
At midnight and at noon, burn agalloch incense.

While reciting the mantra, insert the person's name into the verse; then, lash their effigy with branches of pomegranate. Recite the mantra twenty-one times, lashing once for each repetition, and [the affliction] will be immediately removed.
If the five planets are oppressive and powerful, or if one’s life-force is declining, one should also perform this rite.

The Great Sage’s mantra for pacifying calamities is: *Oṃ sarvatathāgataśrīye svāhā*. The mantra for destroying the disasters caused by the *nakṣatras* and *grahas* is: *Oṃ sarvataraśrīye samaye svāhā*. The mantra for the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper is: *Kāli ke jvaliye paripātha sujñānamaye svāhā*. For incense, use *kunduruka*; the altar may be prepared according to the following layout.
The *Homa Ritual of the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper* was completed on the twenty-seventh day of the third month in the second year of the Kōan era (1279),
transcribed at the quarters of Tōji.
The original manuscript was not clear and contained many errors.

This may be used for collation and verification against the original. Fugohō (Fruit-Jewel), No. 57. On the twelfth day of the sixth month in the second year of Tenmei, the *Jin-yin* year, this was transcribed using the manuscript from Kanchiin of Tōji.

The pen was laid down at the Nan-sam-sha (South Pine House) of the Jijik Kyo-won (Jizōkyō-in). Written by Chirin (48th [generation]). From the *Gansu-ji Shingon-shū* (Collection of Mantras from Gansu Temple):
"The Ritual for the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper, composed by Il-haeng."
Furthermore, this method of pointing to the tail of the Big Dipper is cited here.
This year, I sought out the original text from Chikaku-in and collated it with the national characters (kanji) for publication.

When the aforementioned wooden [relic] was stored in the treasure house of the Kan’gen Gakuin on the second day of the fifth month of the second year of Jōwa (1347), at the Rinka of the Shōon’in in Chōkokuji, Higashiyama, Kyoto.
Recorded by the śramaṇa Kuaidao of the Zongchi Monastery.
